My land is in the North China Plain — flat, with a well for irrigation. I've been farming here since I was a teenager, watching my father do the same rotation year after year: winter wheat, then summer maize on the same plots. That's what I'll do again. Everyone around here does it, the markets are predictable, the inputs are easy to get in town, and I know this system in my sleep.

I have about 8 mu of cultivated land. I'll put all of it into wheat starting in October, then follow with maize on the same ground after the June wheat harvest. No point experimenting at my age — I need reliable income, not surprises. My son moved to the city so I'm managing mostly alone, which means I also need crops I can handle without much hired labor.

For seeds, I buy improved wheat varieties from the village supply cooperative — something like Aikang 58 or whatever the co-op is pushing this year. For maize I'll use a hybrid like Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, same as my neighbors. These aren't my grandfather's seeds but they yield well and I've trusted them for years.

I'll irrigate wheat four times: once at sowing, once before winter, once at jointing, and once at grain-fill. Maize gets three waterings. The water table has been dropping — I've noticed it takes longer to pump now — but I won't cut irrigations. A bad yield is worse than a high electricity bill.

I apply compound fertilizer and urea at rates I've used for the past decade. I spray herbicide in late winter on the wheat, and hit both crops for insects and fungus as needed.
